hypothesis: Who the household is (demographics) and when the snapshot is (calendar) predict 4-week spend.
transformation_description: Baseline: demographic codes, has_demographics, snapshot day index, week-of-year.

hypothesis: Recent purchasing behavior (spend, trip frequency, recency, trends) predicts future 4-week spend far better than demographics alone.
transformation_description: Added RFM features: spend and basket counts in 4/8/12/28/56/112-week windows, total spend, tenure, days since last purchase, average basket size, short/long window trends, active flag, snapshot day/week.
reasoning_summary: Grocery spend is highly autocorrelated: recent spend and trip frequency are the strongest known predictors of near-future spend; recency distinguishes churned households.

hypothesis: How a household shops (department/brand mix, price points, discount usage, purchase regularity, and the 4-week spend lag pattern) predicts its next 4-week spend beyond recent RFM totals.
transformation_description: Added ~70 features to E000-style base: 112d department spend shares, brand share, discount shares, price/unit/line stats, basket-gap stats, week-active share, 4-week lag spend pattern with CV, and snap calendar.
reasoning_summary: E001 showed spend levels dominate; composition and regularity should add signal about whether a household's spend level is stable or a spike, and mix shifts predict level changes.

hypothesis: Combining RFM and shopping-composition features gives the model complementary signals (how much + how) that either alone misses.
transformation_description: Union of E001 RFM features and E002 composition features (merged on household_key, snapshot_day; duplicate spend_total kept once).
reasoning_summary: E001 and E002 were built on different bases; their feature sets are complementary (recency/frequency vs mix/price/discount), so combining them should improve on either.

hypothesis: Beyond recent spend, each household's own 4-week spend at the same position in previous 28-day cycles (especially lag 13 = one year ago), its recency-decayed spend, and basket-level structure predict the next 4-week spend.
transformation_description: E003 features + seasonal 4w lags 1-13 (full windows only), lag11-13 mean/max, lag13 basket count/active flag/ratio, zero-cycle share, exponential decay (tau 28/56), 7/14d spend, basket max/std/top1-share, active-day rate, weekend share.
reasoning_summary: Verified offline that lag13 spend correlates 0.36 and cuts raw lag1 MAE from 84 to 80; households are habitual so same-cycle-last-year spend and decayed recent spend should beat plain window sums.

hypothesis: Marketing exposure predicts future spend: campaign targeting status, coupon redemption history, and the household's share of recent spend on displayed/mailed products carry incremental signal beyond RFM and composition features.
transformation_description: E003 features + 21 marketing features (campaign target counts/recency/active flags, redemption counts/recency, share of spend/lines/baskets on displayed or mailed products over 28/112d, spend share on products displayed in the snapshot's current week).
reasoning_summary: Campaign targets cover 52% of households and displayed-product spend shares are computable for most; promotional responsiveness plausibly drives short-run spend changes that pure RFM misses.

error: exceeded 15 tool calls without calling the evaluation tool

hypothesis: Household-level historical target statistics (past 4-week spend outcomes for the same household, and for households with similar recent spend level or demographics) carry signal beyond current features, improving prediction of future_spend_4w.
transformation_description: E005 features + 8 leak-free target-encoding features computed strictly from earlier snapshots: household mean/count/shrunk mean of past future_spend_4w, spend-bin target mean, global prior, and demographic-group (household size, homeowner, kids) target means.
reasoning_summary: Past realized outcomes of the same household are the most direct evidence of its spend level; grouping by recent-spend bin and demographics pools noisy household estimates. Strictly backward-looking computation avoids leakage.

hypothesis: A household's spend process — the distribution of its rolling 28-day spend windows (mean/std/min/max/median/CV/zero-share), weekly spend level and variability, recent-vs-typical position, and trip cadence (interval stats, phase since last trip, expected trips in next 28d) — predicts next-4-week spend beyond recent spend, seasonal lags, marketing, and target encodings.
transformation_description: E007 features + 23 spend-process/cadence features: rolling 28d window stats sampled every 7d over full history, weekly 7d stats + 13-week slope, recent28 vs typical ratio/difference, and basket-interval cadence features (mean/median/std overall and last-112d, days-since-last, phase = dsl/clipped mean interval, expected trips in next 28d).
reasoning_summary: Recent 4w spend is one noisy draw from each household's own spend distribution; window statistics estimate its baseline level and activity probability, and cadence/phase features estimate whether the next 28 days fall in an active part of the household's shopping cycle.

hypothesis: Recency-weighted (exponentially decayed) spend and trip intensity predicts future 4-week spend better than flat-window aggregates: households whose recent spend (with ~4-week half-life) is high relative to their long-run average will spend more in the next 4 weeks.
transformation_description: E007 features + 18 exponential-decay features: EWMA spend, spend-rate, log-spend and basket counts at half-lives 14/28/56/112 days.
error: key set must equal the canonical train+validation keys (36,426 rows): 9,989 missing, 0 unexpected. Use build_features() to get the keys right.
reasoning_summary: EWMA at 28d half-life is the single best level predictor in inner validation (MAE 69.1 vs 70.2 for spend_112w), so it should add a sharper level signal to the model.

hypothesis: Recency-weighted (exponentially decayed) spend and trip intensity predicts future 4-week spend better than flat window sums: EWMA spend/log-spend/basket rates at half-lives 7-56d, recency of activity, and short-vs-long momentum ratios capture regime shifts.
transformation_description: E007 features + 31 leak-free EWMA features (spend/log-spend/basket EWMA, rates, average-spend-per-active-day, recency, momentum ratios) rebuilt inside build_features, reindexed to view.households to fix E009's missing keys.
reasoning_summary: Exponential decay weights the most recent trips most heavily, so households whose intensity is rising or falling are distinguished from those with identical flat-window totals; momentum ratios directly encode trend.

hypothesis: A household's own realized past 4-week outcomes (recency-weighted EWMA of earlier snapshot targets, zero-window share, recent-window stats) predict its next 4-week spend better than transaction-only features, and a leaner feature set (dropping duplicate/junk columns) reduces noise.
transformation_description: E007 features minus junk/duplicate snapshot-index columns, plus 11 leak-free outcome-history features (EWMA of past realized targets at halflife 1.5/4, zero-window share, min/max/trend/CV of last 3 outcomes, interactions) and raw demographics.
reasoning_summary: Local proxies showed the recency-weighted EWMA of past realized targets alone beats the full E007 ridge fit (64.0 vs 66.2 MAE at snapshot 431), and that a lean core feature set outperforms the full 139-feature table, so adding outcome-history features to a cleaned E007 should improve validation MAE.

hypothesis: A household's own realized past 4-week spend outcomes (consecutive 28d windows): their zero-share, dispersion (std/cv), slope and EWMA — plus trip-cadence reconstruction (expected trips/spend next 4w from inter-purchase gaps × basket size, spend_7d, max_basket_4w, basket-rate ratio) — add predictive signal beyond E007's mean-encoding.
transformation_description: E007 features + 22 leak-free features: outcome series over consecutive prior snapshots (te2_n/mean/med/std/cv/zero/min/max/slope/ewm), all-time and 8w inter-purchase gap stats, expected trips & spend next 4w (28/gap_mean × avg basket), exp_spend_112, spend_7d, nbask_7d, active_7d, max_basket_4w, nbask_ratio_4_28.
reasoning_summary: E011's version of this idea was buggy (corr≈0.01 with target), so the outcome-history hypothesis is untested; zero-share and dispersion of a household's own past 4-week outcomes should sharpen tail predictions, and cadence reconstruction gives a metric-aligned expected-spend estimate.

hypothesis: Store-choice, product-variety/repeat, and basket-composition behavior carries incremental predictive signal beyond E012's RFM/outcome history: spend at the household's main store, 14-day recency spend, distinct products bought, repeat-product share, new-product share, top-product concentration, department entropy, basket size/units, and weekend shopping share each add information about 4-week future spend.
transformation_description: E012 features + 19 store-choice/product-repeat/basket-composition features (main-store 84d share & 28d spend, 14d spend/baskets, distinct products 28d, repeat-product count & spend share 84d, new-product spend share 28d, top1 product share 84d, basket mean spend/units 84d, weekend share, dept entropy 84d).
reasoning_summary: Leak-free partial correlations (controlling E012's strongest columns) show these behavioral features carry incremental signal (e.g. main-store 28d spend +0.088, 14d spend +0.081, new-product share -0.054), so they should add complementary information to the best model.

hypothesis: Store-context trend (main store's recent sales trend and household's share of it), stock-up purchase cycles (share/recency/spacing of >2x-median baskets), and past campaign-response uplift (post-vs-pre campaign spend change) carry incremental signal about future 4-week spend beyond E013's RFM/composition/outcome-history features.
transformation_description: E013 features + 13 batch1 features: st_trend_8w, st_hh_share, st_main_spend_ratio4, stock_share_84, days_since_stock, stock_cycle, bk_p90_ratio, camp_resp, camp_resp_n, resp_TypeA/B/C, camp_resp_last, n_red_active28
error: table_path must be a .parquet file written with DataFrame.to_parquet
reasoning_summary: A household's future spend partly depends on where it shops (a rising main store or high share of a small store's volume) and on recurring stock-up patterns; prior campaign response measures marketing sensitivity, which E013 lacks.

hypothesis: Store-context trend (main store's recent sales trend and household's share of it), stock-up behavior (share of spend in large-basket trips, days since last stock-up), and campaign response history predict future 4-week spend beyond E013 features.
transformation_description: E013 features + 14 batch1 features: st_trend_8w, st_hh_share, st_main_spend_ratio4, stock_share_84, days_since_stock, stock_cycle, bk_p90_ratio, camp_resp* (per campaign type), camp_resp_last, n_red_active28.
reasoning_summary: Stock-up trips temporarily inflate spend and are followed by troughs; a rising main store and a household that responds to campaigns should spend more. E013's store-choice features helped, so store context may add more.

hypothesis: Commodity-level shopping detail predicts future 4-week spend: which specific commodities a household buys (56d shares, 28d spend levels), how recently and how regularly it buys its top staples (days-since/mean-interval for top-8 commodities), and how varied/anchored its baskets are (per-basket commodity diversity, grocery-anchored dwell share) carry incremental signal beyond E013's store/RFM/TE features.
transformation_description: E013 features + 82 new features: cm56_* (24 commodity 56d spend shares), cm28_* (24 commodity 28d spend levels), cd_last_*/cd_int_* (8 commodities × days-since-last & mean purchase interval), bkdiv_28/84 (mean per-basket commodity diversity), dwell_groc84 & bkanchor_groc84 (grocery-anchored dwell shares).
reasoning_summary: E013's department shares (112d) are coarse; commodity-level mix and staple cadence describe what the household will need to restock next, which should sharpen the 4-week spend forecast, especially for regulars.

hypothesis: Within-cycle timing structure predicts future spend: the week-of-cycle pattern of the trailing 28d spend (which of the 4 weeks the household spends in, as shares), trip-gap distribution (mean/median/std/max gap, share of large gaps, longest current streak), fraction of historically zero/low 28d windows, and cohort-relative spend rank predict the next 4-week total beyond E013 features.
transformation_description: E013 features + 28 new: 12 phase weekly spends (3 trailing cycles x 4 weeks) + 4 within-cycle shares, 5 trip-gap stats over 112d, longest gap streak 84d, zero/low window fractions, active days 28d, spend rank pct 28/56d, spend vs cohort median.
reasoning_summary: A household's spend arrives in cycles; where it currently sits in its cycle (week-of-cycle shares, gap since last trip, streak) and how regular its windows are (zero/low fractions) should sharpen the 4-week forecast beyond level and composition features.

hypothesis: Spend dynamics — trend, momentum, acceleration, volatility, pulsing, and trip-timing pressure — predict future 4-week spend beyond the level and composition features in E013/E017.
transformation_description: E013 features + 27 new dynamics features: momentum ratios (s4/lag1, s4 vs 12w, 8w vs 16w), OLS weekly slopes (13w/26w), acceleration, CV13/CV26, top-2-week concentration, zero-run streaks, lag-1 autocorrelation, up/down streak counts, population-relative percentiles (s4, s8), inter-basket gap trend, overdue-next-purchase flag, 7d/14d basket counts, units-per-basket and distinct-products-per-basket trends, weekend/evening shares.
reasoning_summary: E013's features describe how much and what households buy, but not how their spending is changing or timed. Momentum ratios, weekly slopes, acceleration, volatility and zero-run streaks should separate households whose spend is rising/falling or pulsing ahead of a flat 4-week average, and the overdue-purchase flag should capture households whose regular cycle implies a purchase inside the next 4 weeks.

hypothesis: The three sibling branches on E013 carry complementary signals: commodity-level shopping detail (E016), within-cycle timing structure (E017), and spend dynamics (E018). A union of all three should beat each individually.
transformation_description: E013 features + union of E016 batch2 (82 commodity share/inter-purchase features), E017 phase (28 cycle-timing features), E018 dynamics (27 trend/momentum/volatility features) = 317 features, all disjoint from base.
reasoning_summary: Each branch improved MAE on its own (62.47/62.43/62.34 vs 62.53); their feature sets are nearly orthogonal (commodity mix vs cycle phase vs spend dynamics), so the model should gain from all three simultaneously.

hypothesis: The in-store promotional environment a household faces — display and mailer activity at its stores and on the products it buys — carries incremental signal for future 4-week spend beyond E018's behavioral features.
transformation_description: E018 features + 17 display/mailer exposure features: store-weighted counts of displayed/mailer products at the household's stores (4w, 1w, prior-4w), main-store counts, # stores with exposure, product-level display/mailer coverage of the household's recent basket (count and spend share), trends and ratios.
reasoning_summary: Promotional exposure drives purchase timing; households whose usual stores/baskets are heavily promoted may pull purchases forward or defer them, so display/mailer context should add predictive signal beyond behavior-only features.
